1.support: The approach to applying positive end-expiratory pressure in morbidly obese patients is not well defined... We hypothesized that lung recruitment maneuvers and titration of positive end-expiratory pressure were both necessary to improve lung volumes

2.support: The inclusion criteria were as follows: age older than 18 years, BMI more than 35 kg/m2, and absence of a diagnosis of acute respiratory distress syndrome as defined by the Berlin criteria
2.location: Page 2, MATERIAL AND METHODS, Population and Study Protocol

3.support: Critically ill, mechanically ventilated morbidly obese (body mass index > 35 kg/m2) patients (n = 14)... ICU patients were screened from surgical, neurologic, and medical ICUs

4.support: The report states fourteen patients met all inclusion criteria and were enrolled, but does not report how many patients were screened or whether eligible patients declined consent, so enrollment of all eligible participants cannot be determined.

5.support: Sample size calculations showed that 13 patients were needed in order to detect a predicted increase in EELV of at least 300 mL ± 300 mL after PEEP titration with a power of 0.9

6.support: PEEP was progressively increased in a stepwise manner until it matched or was slightly greater than the Pes at end expiration... RMs were performed in a stepwise fashion... The total duration of the RM was 2 minutes.
6.location: Page 2, PEEP Titration Techniques and RMs

7.support: EELV was estimated by the 10% oxygen/nitrogen wash-in/wash-out technique... EELV was measured twice for every study step, and the results were averaged. Gas exchange was measured through arterial blood gas analysis.
7.location: Page 2-3, EELV Estimation and Gas Exchange

8.support: The report does not describe any blinding of outcome assessors; the physiologic measurements (EELV, transpulmonary pressures, blood gases) were objective, but whether assessors were masked is not reported.

9.support: Fourteen patients (eight men, six women) met all the inclusion criteria and were enrolled in the study... ZEEP maneuver was performed only on four patients, as deemed safe by the attending physician.

10.support: The overall differences in respiratory and hemodynamic variables at different PEEP levels were assessed by repeated-measures analysis of variance. Single changes... were compared using post hoc Holm-Bonferroni corrections

11.support: Measurements were obtained at the baseline positive end-expiratory pressure set by the clinicians, at zero positive end-expiratory pressure, at best positive end-expiratory pressure... before and after a recruitment maneuver
11.location: Page 1, Abstract (Interventions); page 2, Population and Study Protocol

12.support: The intervention (esophageal-pressure-guided PEEP titration and recruitment maneuvers) was applied at the individual patient level, so this item does not apply.
12.location: Page 2, PEEP Titration Techniques and RMs

nih.rationale: The rating is driven down from Good by item 4 (cannot determine whether all eligible patients were enrolled; only 14 patients from unspecified screening), item 8 (no blinding of outcome assessors reported, and treating clinicians were necessarily aware of the intervention), and item 11 (outcomes were not measured multiple times before and after the intervention in an interrupted time-series design; gas exchange was not even measured at every step, as the authors acknowledge: 'gas exchange evaluation could not be performed at every study step'). The design is also nonrandomized crossover within patients, vulnerable to time-related confounding. Strengths keeping the rating at Fair rather than Poor include a clear objective (item 1), prespecified eligibility criteria (item 2), an a priori sample size calculation with 90% power (item 5), a clearly and consistently delivered intervention (item 6), valid and repeated objective outcome measures (item 7), complete follow-up with no apparent loss (item 9), and appropriate repeated-measures statistics with p values (item 10).
